message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) the melting/freezing point of pure water drops to roughly **–2 °C**.  
In other words, ice will melt (or water will freeze) at about –2 °C when the surrounding pressure is only 10 kPa. This is a slight depression compared with the 0 °C freezing point at 1 atm, reflecting the negative slope of the ice–water coexistence line in the phase diagram.
